titleEn: Choosing a way to learn Japanese
titleTh: เลือกวิธีเรียนภาษาญี่ปุ่น
scenarioSentences: You want to learn Japanese.
Your friend Aiko is Japanese.
You are not sure how to start.
You do not have much money.
You ask Aiko for advice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Aiko, I want to learn Japanese. What's the best way to start?

dialogue.speaker: Aiko
dialogue.text: You could use an app, join a class, or find a tutor.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: An app is free, but I might give up quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Aiko
dialogue.text: True. A tutor is faster, but it's expensive.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What about the evening class at the community center?

dialogue.speaker: Aiko
dialogue.text: It's forty dollars a month, twice a week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's cheaper than a tutor. Will I get enough speaking practice?

dialogue.speaker: Aiko
dialogue.text: Probably not. If you take the class, I'll practice with you on weekends.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks! I'll sign up tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Aiko
dialogue.text: Great. Let's meet on Saturday for our first chat.

titleEn: Asking a neighbor to take a package
titleTh: ฝากเพื่อนบ้านรับพัสดุแทน
scenarioSentences: You ordered a new desk online.
It arrives tomorrow afternoon.
You will be at work all day.
Ms. Nolan lives next door.
She usually works from home.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Ms. Nolan. Could I ask you a small favor?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Nolan
dialogue.text: Of course. What do you need?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: A package is coming tomorrow, but I'll be at work until six.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Nolan
dialogue.text: No problem. I'm home all day. How big is it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's a desk, so the box is quite heavy.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Nolan
dialogue.text: Then I'll ask the driver to carry it into my hallway.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll put a note on my door with your apartment number.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Nolan
dialogue.text: Good idea. When will you pick it up?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Is seven o'clock okay? I'll come straight after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Nolan
dialogue.text: Seven is fine. I'll see you then.

titleEn: Making a farewell card for a coworker
titleTh: ทำการ์ดอำลาให้เพื่อนร่วมงาน
scenarioSentences: Your coworker Sara leaves next Friday.
She has been here for five years.
You want to give her a card.
Ivan sits near you.
You ask him to help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ivan, Sara's last day is Friday. Should we make her a card?

dialogue.speaker: Ivan
dialogue.text: Yes, definitely. Who should sign it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Everyone on our floor, I think. That's about twenty people.

dialogue.speaker: Ivan
dialogue.text: I'll take it around the office on Wednesday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Should we buy her a gift too?

dialogue.speaker: Ivan
dialogue.text: Maybe. People could give a few dollars each.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: She loves the plants on her desk. How about a small one?

dialogue.speaker: Ivan
dialogue.text: Perfect. It's cheaper than flowers and it lasts longer.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll pick one up on Thursday and buy the card today.

dialogue.speaker: Ivan
dialogue.text: And I'll collect the money and signatures. She'll be so surprised.

titleTh: สมัครเข้ากลุ่มเดินป่าวันหยุด
scenarioSentences: You want to get more exercise.
A local hiking group meets every Sunday.
Sienna leads the group.
You have never hiked before.
You call her with some questions.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Sienna, I'd like to join the hiking group, but I'm a beginner.

dialogue.speaker: Sienna
dialogue.text: That's fine. Have you done any hiking before?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not really. I walk to work, but that's all.

dialogue.speaker: Sienna
dialogue.text: Then start with our easy walk next Sunday. It's about two hours.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sounds good. What should I bring?

dialogue.speaker: Sienna
dialogue.text: Water, a snack, and a rain jacket. Good shoes are the most important.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I only have running shoes. Are they okay?

dialogue.speaker: Sienna
dialogue.text: For the easy walk, yes. You should buy proper hiking boots later.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Where do we meet?

dialogue.speaker: Sienna
dialogue.text: At the park gate at eight. See you there!

titleTh: ติดตั้งเครื่องพิมพ์เครื่องใหม่
scenarioSentences: You bought a printer yesterday.
It will not connect to your laptop.
Your essay is due tomorrow morning.
Your friend Victor is good with computers.
You call him for help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Victor, my new printer won't connect to my laptop. Can you help?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Sure. Are you trying to connect without a cable?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. I've tried three times, but the laptop can't find it.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: First, turn both of them off and wait a minute.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Done. They're back on now.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Is the printer showing up now?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, still nothing. And I have to print my essay tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Then use the cable in the box. Wireless can take longer to set up.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Oh, I found it. It's printing now!

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Great. I'll come over this weekend and fix the wireless for you.

titleEn: Getting a flu shot at the clinic
titleTh: ไปฉีดวัคซีนไข้หวัดใหญ่ที่คลินิก
scenarioSentences: Many people at work have the flu.
You want a flu shot this year.
You feel a little nervous.
Nurse Kaur works at the clinic.
You ask her some questions.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Nurse Kaur. I'd like a flu shot, but I'm a bit worried.

dialogue.speaker: Nurse Kaur
dialogue.text: That's normal. What are you worried about?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Is it safe? I've never had one before.

dialogue.speaker: Nurse Kaur
dialogue.text: Yes, it's very safe. Millions of people get one every year.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Will I feel sick afterwards?

dialogue.speaker: Nurse Kaur
dialogue.text: Some people get a sore arm for a day or two. That's normal.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Can I still go to the gym tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Nurse Kaur
dialogue.text: You should rest tonight. Light exercise is fine tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: All right, I'll have it today, then.

dialogue.speaker: Nurse Kaur
dialogue.text: Good. Please roll up your sleeve and sit here.

titleTh: สมัครร้องเพลงกับคณะประสานเสียงชุมชน
scenarioSentences: You love singing at home.
A community choir meets on Wednesdays.
Ms. Abara leads the choir.
You are not sure you sing well.
You talk to her after a concert.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ms. Abara, I enjoyed the concert. I'd love to join the choir.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Abara
dialogue.text: Wonderful! Have you sung in a choir before?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Never. I only sing at home, and I'm not sure I sing well.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Abara
dialogue.text: Don't worry. Most of our members started as beginners.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Do I have to do a test?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Abara
dialogue.text: No test. Just come to a free practice and see if you like it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds less scary. What time does it start?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Abara
dialogue.text: Seven o'clock on Wednesday, in the hall behind the library.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll be there. Should I bring anything?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Abara
dialogue.text: Just water. We'll give you the music.

titleTh: วางแผนเส้นทางขับรถเที่ยว
scenarioSentences: You and Nadia are driving to the beach.
You are leaving on Saturday morning.
There are two possible roads.
The highway is faster but boring.
You discuss the route together.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Nadia, which road should we take on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: The highway is the fastest. We'd be there in three hours.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True, but the coast road has amazing views.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: How much longer does it take?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: About an hour more, maybe a bit longer if there's traffic.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: That's okay if we leave early. The drive should be fun too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We could stop at a fishing town for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: Good idea. I've heard the seafood there is great.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So let's take the coast road and leave at seven.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll bring snacks and you choose the music.

titleEn: Teaching Grandma to use a smartphone
titleTh: สอนคุณยายใช้สมาร์ตโฟน
scenarioSentences: Grandma got her first smartphone last week.
She wants to message the family.
She also wants to see family photos.
You visit her on Saturday.
You offer to help her.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Grandma, shall we look at your new phone together?

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I can't even find the messages.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's this green icon. Tap it, then choose a name.

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: Oh, I see. Can I send a message to your mother?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sure. Type your message here and press the arrow.

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: I did it! Now, how do I see the photos she sends?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: They're here, in the photo album.

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: Lovely. Could I also see your faces when we talk?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, with a video call. Let's practice on Sunday when Mom calls.

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: Wonderful. I'll write the steps down.

titleEn: Giving directions to a lost tourist
titleTh: บอกทางนักท่องเที่ยวที่หลงทาง
scenarioSentences: You are walking through the old town.
A tourist, Mrs. Hart, looks lost.
She is holding a big suitcase.
She asks you for help.
She needs to find the train station.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello. You look a bit lost. Can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hart
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I need to get to the train station.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's not far. You can walk there in about ten minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hart
dialogue.text: My suitcase is very heavy, though. Is there a bus?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: There's no bus, but the tram stops just across the road.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hart
dialogue.text: How often does it come?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Every five minutes. Take number three and get off after two stops.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hart
dialogue.text: Do I buy a ticket on the tram?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, use the machine at the stop. It takes cards.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Hart
dialogue.text: Thank you so much. I'll take the tram, then.
